newsitem.title: USA: Polo Ralph Lauren could defy sour IPO market.
newsitem.headline: Polo Ralph Lauren could defy sour IPO market.

text.p: Ending months of Wall Street speculation, designer Polo Ralph Lauren Corp has decided to go public, filing for a $600 million initial public offering on Wednesday.
Analysts say all the conditions are right for the offering of the New York-based designer despite a weary IPO market.
"This is going to be a very sought-after offering, no doubt," said Manish Shah, president of the IPO Maven.

New York-based designer Ralph Lauren launched his first brand, Polo, in 1967 with a collection of men's ties and then moved into menswear. The now-famous logo of a polo player astride a horse appeared in 1971.
Since then, the designer has moved into women's clothing, wear, home products such as towels and bedding and accessories including eyeglasses, jewelry, handbags and luggage.
Sales have shown impressive growth -- topping $1.0 billion in fiscal 1996, according to the regulatory filing.
Income from operations has grown at a 19.1 percent compound annual rate from $63.2 million in fiscal 1992 to $127.1 million in fiscal 1996.

Analysts said the offering could benefit from the IPO market, which now favors large blue-chip-type IPOs and the deal's strong underwriting team. The IPO will be lead-managed by Goldman Sachs, which owns 28 percent of Ralph Lauren. Morgan Stanley and Merrill Lynch will also underwrite the deal.
The company proposes to trade on the New York Stock Exchange under the symbol "RL".
